Repository: anit0607/ai-journey-studio
Commit: 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1
Note: docs/build-notes/studio-progress.md

## Verified progress
- Documented assistant-observed database configuration, scheduler behavior and provider status on 25 October 2026; these are system observations, not the owner's personal experiences or feelings.
- Verified that the existing Neon Free account had a monthly allowance of 100 compute-unit hours per project.
- Verified that the production endpoint was configured with both minimum and maximum compute at 0.25 compute units and a five-minute autosuspend delay.
- Documented two sources of database reads in the previous setup: two-minute integration requests and five-second signed-in dashboard polling.
- Updated signed integration-request handling to validate the request and return before database access when outside the configured source-intake and publishing windows.
- Updated source intake to use hourly windows and publication handling to use exact configured windows.
- Updated background dashboard polling to pause when the page is hidden or unfocused, or after 60 seconds without activity; polling remains available when the page is active and recently used.
- Verified that fresh Neon provider observations reported at 04:10:55 UTC and 04:12:20 UTC on 25 October 2026 showed the production endpoint as SUSPENDED; these are reported observation times, not suspension event timestamps.
- Verified that a fresh Neon observation reported at 04:14:50 UTC again showed SUSPENDED; a separate Upstash metadata observation recorded the scheduled 04:12 integration wake as SUCCESS, without establishing a response body, HTTP status code or request-level SQL trace.
- Documented that the observation used provider status reads without SQL queries, manual resume or settings changes during the observation window.
- Documented that the verification used the existing connected account and Free plan, without a paid-plan upgrade.
- Documented the limits of this result: the checks establish endpoint state at the observed times, not uninterrupted sleep, measured monthly compute savings, guaranteed use within the Free allowance or successful LinkedIn publication.
- Documented that the commit linked below identifies the implementation change; the endpoint settings and runtime observations above come from separately inspected provider receipts, not from treating a commit link as runtime proof.

## Evidence
- https://github.com/anit0607/ai-journey-studio/commit/e2a608b9f7a9e1dfde4f96709e8cb47a182819ff

Studio progress on 25 October 2026 in the repository anit0607/ai-journey-studio documented detailed observations and configuration adjustments regarding database usage and autosuspend operation with a Neon Free account. The documented points include:

- The Neon Free account allowed 100 compute-unit hours per project monthly.
- The production endpoint was set to both minimum and maximum of 0.25 compute units with a five-minute autosuspend delay.
- Database reads originated from two-minute interval integration requests and five-second interval signed-in dashboard polling.
- Integration-request handling was updated to validate requests and skip database access when requests fell outside configured intake and publishing windows.
- Source intake operated using hourly windows, while publications used exact configured windows.
- Background dashboard polling was configured to pause when the page was hidden, unfocused, or inactive for more than 60 seconds; polling remained active when the page was in use.
- Observations at 04:10:55 UTC, 04:12:20 UTC, and 04:14:50 UTC reported the production endpoint as SUSPENDED without SQL queries or manual intervention.
- Upstash metadata recorded a successful scheduled integration wake at 04:12 without revealing response or SQL trace data.
- No paid-plan upgrade was used; all verifications were within the existing connected Free plan.
- The documented verification specified limits: endpoint state was established only at observed timestamps, without claims about uninterrupted sleep duration, exact monthly compute savings, guaranteed Free plan compliance, or confirmation of LinkedIn publication success.
- The linked commit e2a608b9f7a9e1dfde4f96709e8cb47a182819ff identified the implementation change but was distinct from observed runtime data, which were based on provider receipts and system observations.

High-frequency dashboard polling can easily push a Neon Free database over its 100 compute-unit hour monthly limit without clear benefit. In AI-Journey-Studio’s setup, they tackled this by adapting background polling behavior to reduce unnecessary database calls.

Specifically, the dashboard now pauses its five-second refresh cycle whenever the browser tab is hidden, unfocused, or idle for more than 60 seconds. Polling resumes only when the page is active and recently used. Alongside this, the system checks incoming integration requests against hourly configured windows, stopping early if outside allowed intake or publish times—so no needless database access happens.

Provider observations confirmed that during these idle times, the production database endpoint entered a SUSPENDED state without any SQL queries or manual intervention. This shows autosuspend worked under the Free plan configuration with minimum/maximum compute set to 0.25 units and a five-minute autosuspend delay.

These spot checks don’t guarantee continuous savings or exact compute usage over a month, but they do demonstrate a practical way to keep polling efficient and help avoid hitting free-tier limits.

If you’re building agent-driven dashboards, try having your agent list all services contacted outside configured windows and pause their polling paths before hitting the database—without skipping request validation.

Source: GitHub repository anit0607/ai-journey-studio, commit 0453b6c7d36a76b3bd306c02dc0c9c854db452d1, documented 25 October 2026

### LinkedIn

High-frequency polling can quietly drain your database’s free compute budget without visible benefit. In one recent setup, a database endpoint had a five-minute autosuspend setting, but the signed-in dashboard refreshed every five seconds, creating a mismatch.

To fix this, polling was updated to pause automatically when the browser tab is hidden, unfocused, or idle for more than 60 seconds—resuming only when the page is active again. Scheduled integration requests also got a gate: they validate timing and stop early if outside allowed intake or publish windows, avoiding unnecessary database hits.

Later observations confirmed the database production endpoint entered a SUSPENDED state during idle periods without any SQL queries or manual intervention. This shows autosuspend working as intended within the Free plan’s 0.25 compute unit min/max settings and a five-minute delay.

This spot check doesn’t prove continuous sleep or exact compute savings, but it does highlight a practical way to reduce wasteful queries.

If you’re building agent-driven services, try this: for each background task, list all contacted services outside allowed time windows and pause their database calls—without skipping validation. The quieter your system when idle, the better.
